root_cause.text: The `fpu_vstl()` function in the s390 FPU subsystem uses inline assembly constraints that specify a 1-byte write (`*(u8 *)vxr`), which causes Clang's KMSAN instrumentation to only unpoison 1 byte at compile-time, whereas the `vstl` instruction actually writes a variable number of bytes at runtime depending on the `index` argument.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff for `arch/s390/include/asm/fpu-insn.h` adds manual calls to `kmsan_unpoison_memory(vxr, size)` in `fpu_vstl()`. This is supported by the commit message, which explains that clang compile-time constraint evaluation generates a call to `__msan_instrument_asm_store` with a 1-byte size because the runtime `index` argument determining the actual write size of the `vstl` instruction is unknown at compile-time.

intent_record.intent_summary: Include <linux/kmsan.h> to enable KMSAN instrumentation support.
intent_record.what: Added the #include <linux/kmsan.h> directive to the header file.
intent_record.how: Provides the necessary declarations and macros for Kernel Memory Sanitizer (KMSAN) to instrument this translation unit.

intent_record.intent_summary: Unpoison memory modified by inline assembly in fpu_vstl to prevent false positive KMSAN warnings.
intent_record.what: Added a call to kmsan_unpoison_memory after the inline assembly block in the fpu_vstl function.
intent_record.how: This informs the KernelMemorySanitizer (KMSAN) that the memory modified by the inline assembly has been initialized, preventing false positive warnings.

intent_record.intent_summary: Notify KMSAN that the memory written by fpu_vstl has been initialized to prevent false positive warnings.

intent_record.how: It marks the memory range modified by the assembly instruction as initialized, preventing KMSAN from triggering false positive uninitialized memory warnings.
